note: Forward-and-back basic danced solo. Counts 4 and 8 are held, not stepped — the pause is part of the step and learners who fill it are dancing a different rhythm.

measurability.rationale: Weight transfer produces large thigh-orientation and knee-flexion changes. Step direction is fronto-parallel to the camera. No turns in the basic.
riskFlags: Step size is small relative to hip-hop; amplitude thresholds must be calibrated against real takes before shipping (plan §12.4).
measurability.tierStatus: UNVERIFIED (M-F-144 KARAR 2): the measurement commissioned to confirm or lower this tier returned overlap at all three foot levels and could not decide, for a named structural reason (no positive control — see harvestProbe4_footLevel.whyTheMeasurementCannotDecide). Tier A is the INHERITED value, not a re-confirmed one. Do not cite it as measured.

scoring.freeJointsRationale: Arm carriage in solo salsa varies widely between schools. V1 scores footwork and timing only, and says so to the user (plan C-014).

errors.note: Marking the step with the foot without committing weight. The defining beginner fault in every social dance and the reason the basic is scored on weight, not foot position.
Stepping on 4 turns the salsa basic into a march. Detecting it needs the hold to be an explicit phase, which is why hold_4 exists.
Only meaningful once mirroring is resolved on the reference side — see catalogue §6.0 and C-005. A mirror error here would blame the learner for our own bug.
Suppressed when TimingSummary.suggestsCalibrationIssue is true — a large, tight bias is uncalibrated audio, not a dragging dancer (plan §9.2).

harvestProbe.question: Is the basic already in the 5 salsa clips harvested for the shines? (cheap check before a targeted harvest)
harvestProbe.criteria: Taken from THIS step's own config, not invented: (a) >=2 plateaus per cycle of >=7 phase bins — hold_4.minDurationMs 120ms on a ~1.1s cycle at 64 bins, and this file's own note 'Counts 4 and 8 are held, not stepped'; (b) sagittal thigh excursion >=12deg — fwd_step/back_step travel, against the shine's MEASURED ceiling of 4.0deg.
harvestProbe.result: 0 candidate windows across 4 probeable sources. Closest was bqoNqA2hmE4 (the '5 FOOTWORK/Shine Steps' compilation): thigh excursion 20.78deg CLEARS the travel criterion but only 1 plateau, not 2. The 2x-harmonic hypothesis (that its 1.47s period was a half cycle hiding the second plateau) was tested and REFUTED: at 2.94s the cycle yields 0 plateaus and an absurd 137.5deg excursion, i.e. it averages two different steps rather than one longer one.
harvestProbe.negativeControl: PASSED — the detector flagged none of the 3 known shine segments as basic (a detector that fires everywhere measures nothing).
harvestProbe.measuredMethodLimit: IMPORTANT, this bounds the conclusion: the movement isolator finds only ~1 usable window per clip (2 in the 16-minute compilation, one of which fails the camera gate) because it searches for SUSTAINED periodic stretches. A compilation that demonstrates five steps briefly each does not present them as five windows. So the honest claim is 'ss_basic is not in the windows this pipeline surfaces', NOT 'ss_basic is not in this footage'.
harvestProbe.verdict: TARGETED HARVEST REQUIRED — ss_basic cannot be built from the existing pool. Search terms should target single-step basic tutorials ('salsa basic step solo', 'forward and back basic'), not compilations.

harvestProbe2_targeted.verdict: 0 basic candidates. ss_basic still has no reference and the lesson stays locked.
harvestProbe2_targeted.structuralLimitA_windowLength: MEASURED: movement_isolator's default window_s=6.0 combined with its own `hi = min(max_period_s*fps, win//3)` rule caps the SEARCHABLE period at ~1.99s. A salsa basic spans 8 beats and can cycle in 3-5s, so the isolator cannot see it BY CONSTRUCTION. Proof: Ballroom Feed yields 0 windows at window_s=6/12 and 1 window at 18 (period 2.97s). This is the other face of the C-102 limit — there short segments were invisible, here long cycles are. NOT a new cutter class: a parameter of the existing one. Permanent change is a coordinator call (movement_isolator is vendored, family-wide).
harvestProbe2_targeted.structuralLimitB_plateauLevel: MEASURED and more fundamental: 3 of 3 measurable sources show ZERO plateaus, including one whose travel amplitude clearly separates it from the shines (13.8-18.9deg vs the shines' 1.4-5.3deg). The plateau detector reads the summed speed of 8 LEG-ANGLE joints; this step's config declares its hold at FOOT-CONTACT level ('Counts 4 and 8 are held, not stepped'). Those are not the same measurement: on count 4 the foot stops while hips and weight keep moving, so an angle-speed detector sees no pause. Negative control still passes (it does not flag the shines either), so the detector is consistent — it is measuring the wrong LEVEL, not measuring badly.
harvestProbe2_targeted.openQuestion: Limit (b) raises a tier question this session did not decide: if ss_basic's defining feature is a foot-contact hold, and foot-contact timing is exactly why Running Man is Tier C (toe landmarks least reliable in markerless single-camera), then ss_basic's `measurability.tier: A` may be optimistic. Raised to the coordinator, not resolved here.

analysisWindow.$comment: M-F-144 KARAR 1. The isolator's `hi = win//3` rule is NOT relaxed — it is an honest ACF constraint (a periodicity claim needs >=3 cycles inside the window, M-C-25). Instead the WINDOW is lengthened, and the length is derived from this step's own count structure plus a MEASURED teaching period.
analysisWindow.expectedPeriodBasis: MEASURED on 9NZp9_GuKrE (Ballroom Feed, 'Forward & Back') — the only harvested source where an 8-count cycle resolved at all. Consistent with this step's beats:8 and with the high end of the disputed BPM range (8 beats / 2.97s = 161 BPM). NOT a guess: the number came out of the isolator, and if a later harvest measures a different teaching period this field moves with it.
analysisWindow.windowDerivation: 3x is arithmetically enough (win//3 >= expectedPeriod needs window >= 3*2.97 = 8.9s) but was MEASURED INSUFFICIENT: at window_s=12 (4 cycles) the same source still scored periodicity 0.49 and was rejected; at 18 (6 cycles) it scored 0.51 and passed. So the binding constraint is not the lag ceiling but the ACF's signal-to-noise, which improves with cycle count. 18s ~= 6x expectedPeriod.
analysisWindow.measuredLimitItFixes: With the family default window_s=6.0 this step is INVISIBLE by construction: hi = win//3 caps the searchable period near 1.99s while an 8-count salsa cycle runs 3-5s. C-104 limit (a) — the other face of C-102 (there short segments were invisible, here long cycles).
analysisWindow.familyDefaultUnchanged: window_s=6.0 stays the family default and is correct for short movements; this is a per-step declaration, and movement_isolator.py itself is NOT modified (window_s was already a parameter) so the vendored copy stays byte-identical to its pin and --drift-check stays clean.
analysisWindow.measuredEffect: APPLIED AND IT WORKS, but it did not rescue this step's candidates. Proof it works: at the family default the isolator surfaced no window longer than ~2s in the targeted sources; with windowSeconds=18 it surfaced periods of 2.74s and 3.10s in Ns5TaVGv6uY — i.e. exactly the 8-count range that was invisible before. Proof it did not rescue: both candidates fail a SECOND, independent gate (see harvestProbe3).

harvestProbe3_reevaluation.instruction: M-F-144 KARAR 1: re-evaluate Ballroom Feed + Dance Dojo with the declared window. No new harvest — the round's data was kept.
harvestProbe3_reevaluation.result: Still 0 basic candidates. The window fix is real but a second gate stops each of them, and the two reasons are different:
harvestProbe3_reevaluation.9NZp9_GuKrE_BallroomFeed: CAMERA ANGLE, not window. Movement window found at 18s (period 2.97s) but the camera gate yields ZERO clean windows: torso yaw median 54.1deg folded, only 14.3% of frames within 15deg and 25.8% within 35deg. The instructor teaches at an oblique angle. This is the gate working as designed (C-041: 30-60deg is the enemy), not a limit to fix.
harvestProbe3_reevaluation.Ns5TaVGv6uY_DanceDojo: NON-OVERLAP. Camera profile is clean (yaw median 7.7deg, 66% within 15deg) and the 18s window surfaced 8 movement windows including 2.74s and 3.10s periods — but NONE of them intersects a camera-clean stretch. The clean stretches and the moving stretches are in different parts of the video. Same class as M-C-16: optimising one criterion and filtering by the other is not the same as optimising over what satisfies both.
harvestProbe3_reevaluation.conclusion: ss_basic remains unbuildable from all footage harvested so far. Three independent obstacles were measured across the two rounds: material without sustained periodicity (Salsaventura), oblique camera (Ballroom Feed), movement/camera non-overlap (Dance Dojo), plus the two structural limits already recorded.

harvestProbe4_footLevel.verdict: NEITHER branch of the hüküm holds: (a) is NO (ankle does not separate) and (b) is also NO (the toe does not separate either). All three foot levels overlap with the control.
harvestProbe4_footLevel.whyTheMeasurementCannotDecide: This is the honest limit, and it is structural rather than a matter of trying harder: there is NO POSITIVE CONTROL. I am looking for the signature of a hold without possessing one verified example of the basic — the reference I would need is the very thing being sought. So an overlap cannot distinguish 'these segments contain no hold' (likely: the strongest candidate is titled Basic VARIATIONS) from 'my measure cannot see a hold that is there'. Breaking the circle needs either a human eye confirming one segment IS the basic, or footage clean enough to build a reference from.
harvestProbe4_footLevel.tierDecision: NOT CHANGED and NOT confirmed. measurability.tier stays A but is now marked unverified below — the measurement asked to settle it came back unable to. Deciding either way on this data would be inventing a verdict.
